note: Machine-readable rule registry. This is the only place a rule is defined. PIPELINE/20-RULES.md is rendered from it, and TOOLING/gate.py enforces the ones with a check. To add a rule, add it here, run pipeline.py render, then run the gate on a known-good file so you know the check does not misfire.

severity_levels.block: gate exits non-zero and the file cannot be delivered
severity_levels.warn: gate reports it, delivery is a judgement call, record the reason in DELIVERY-LOG.md
severity_levels.manual: no automated check exists, a human must confirm it and say so

scopes.all: every file that leaves this repo
scopes.outward: files a client, reviewer, hiring team or vendor receives
scopes.doc: long form: reviews, scopes, reports, articles
scopes.internal: repo-only notes, session logs, state files

rules.text: No em dashes in anything owner-facing. Use a comma, a colon, or a full stop and a new sentence.
No word from banned_words.txt. The list is taken literally on LinkedIn, with the technical exceptions in voice_lint.py allowed only in doc and email profiles.

Never name tomicialgraphics, or any repository URL, account name, handle or email variant built from it, in anything a client, reviewer, hiring team or vendor receives. Pinned revisions are identified to outsiders by commit SHA and file SHA-256 only.
olusanyatimothy54@gmail.com is the only outbound address. Never use tomicialgraphics@gmail.com and never present it as the owner's address.
No local machine paths in a deliverable. No C:\Users, no file:/// URLs, no sandbox paths. Anything the reader cannot open is noise.
No fabricated numbers, rates, sample sizes or results. Only runs that happened, with the run next to the number. When there is no run, ship the method and say so.
rules.verify_with: Every figure in the file traces to a file, a command, or a run recorded in DELIVERY-LOG.md. If it cannot, delete the figure.

rules.text: Every post ships a recommended headline and subheadline pair, plus two alternative pairs.
The headline is under 120 characters, carries the claim, and is never a question. The first line must be incomplete without the second.
Headline plus subheadline are complete inside 200 characters, because that is what shows before the see-more cut.
One boxed phrase per card, one to three words, on a single line, never opening line one. Give the primary box and one alternative.
The box passes the portability test. If the phrase could headline a different post by a different writer, it is wrong. Box the quantity or the failure verb, never the topic.
rules.verify_with: Swap the box into three other posts from the INDEX. If it fits any of them, replace it.

rules.text: Hashtags must be ones actually in use on LinkedIn in this lane, checked against PIPELINE/registry/hashtags.json. Three to five, on the final line. Never invent a tag, never quote a follower count.
Every post names the template it was built on, from the fourteen in DAILY CONTENT/post_templates.txt, and the file records which one.
Everything ships through the human gate. voice_lint minus the gate must be 0 errors, and the human gate must score 90 or above with 0 errors.
Deliverables end on a statement, not a question. A light offer is allowed in a warm reply.
Read the profile of the person before writing a word to them or about them. Name, role, their actual argument, and something only they said.
No links in cold comments. Links are allowed in a warm reply, or where one was already posted.
Nothing goes to a live Upwork or LinkedIn account without owner approval. Drafts are drafts.
Client and reviewer work stays private to that person until they agree otherwise. Findings go to them first, as a file plus a SHA-256, never as a repository link.
Never claim a fix is fixed. Until the post-fix run is in hand, the patch is under test.
Every session writes its own log at SESSION_LOG/SESSION_LOG_<date>.md, recording each instruction, each decision, each artifact with its path, and the open loops.
Every delivered file is journalled in STATE/DELIVERY-LOG.md with its path, SHA-256, gate result, and who it went to. If it is not in the log, it is not delivered.
A post is not ready until its row exists in VERIFIED_POSTS/INDEX.md.
No PII in a public link. The repo is public. Confirm with the owner before committing a new resume, address, phone number or document.
Card geometry and colour are locked. Per-article changes are copy and a generated background only. No AI-generated face of the owner, ever.
rules.verify_with: Compare against the three approved cards in visual_and_hook_spec.md part 4.

rules.text: Every deliverable states what it is, who it is for, and what the reader should do next, in the file itself, not in the chat. A comment or a DM from 2026-11-10 also carries sources_read:, because every link a post attaches is read before the comment is written (owner instruction 2026-11-09). The value is read: <what it was, the date>, or none: nothing attached, or blocked: <why it will not open, what the comment claims without it>. A link that turns out to be a landing page, a waitlist or a listing is still read and still reported as read, with what it turned out to be.
rules.source: owner instruction 2026-11-06, this restructure; owner question 2026-11-09 on reading attached links, then 'please always read it' the same day

rules.text: Read the rules end to end before writing a deliverable, not after. The gate exists to catch what reading missed, not to replace reading.
rules.verify_with: pipeline.py start has been run in this session, and the read order in PIPELINE/00-START.md was followed.

rules.text: Nothing is sent on the owner's behalf. Every send is the owner's action; the agent drafts, gates, and hands over.
A skill or tool that is not in this repo, or not in the EMPIRE, does not get imported into a deliverable. If it is missing, say it is missing.
rules.verify_with: Every capability claimed in a deliverable maps to a file or a run in this repo.

rules.text: Dates and times are stated in WAT and written as 6 Nov 2026. No relative dates in a file that will outlive the week.

Every post goes out with a first comment carrying the AI Red Team Playbook link, from 2026-11-09 until the repository reaches 1,000 stars. The comment earns the link by naming the file that answers that post's point; it is never a bare link drop, and the star count is never quoted.
rules.verify_with: The post's front matter first_comment names the comment file, and that file holds the text that goes under it.

rules.text: A filename typed into pasted text autolinks to an address that does not exist. Anything a human copies into LinkedIn names the file without its extension, and the working URL, where one is allowed, carries the path. Learned twice: a .zip and a .md both turned into dead links inside a comment.

A post that rests on a fact which moves is checked the same day, and the file says which fact and where it was checked. A number in a screenshot can be right on Monday and wrong on Tuesday, and a comment written from it is dated either way. Where the post makes no checkable claim, say so with opinion: rather than leaving the field out.
rules.source: owner question 2026-11-09, the Nvidia repricing check

rules.text: Two substantive exchanges per person per thread, then stop. The other person keeps the last substantive word, whether or not they use it. A third reply is an argument, and an argument under somebody else's post is read as a fight rather than as a point.

A claim about somebody else's system names the version and the surface it was tested on. A proof that runs on an internal path is not a capability: it says the code does the thing, not that anyone can reach it. Say which, every time, because the difference is the whole finding.
rules.source: FORAY correspondence, 2026-11-09, the Tier-2 reachability correction

rules.text: Every hash, byte count and word count quoted to an outside reader is recomputed from the file in the same command that writes the letter, and the delivery log row carries the same value. A hash copied from an earlier message is a claim about a file that may have changed since.

A question the owner has answered twice is not asked a third time. Once he has chosen, the choice is the working assumption, and re-raising it spends his attention on a decision already made. Record the choice and the date instead.
rules.source: owner instruction pattern, November 2026, the Drive ownership caveat

rules.text: A direct question from a reader is answered within a day, or it is acknowledged with the day it will be answered. The queue lives in STATE/REPLY-QUEUE.md with the date received and the date due, so an unanswered question is visible rather than forgotten. A question that arrives on a Friday may be answered on Monday, and it still gets a row.
rules.source: owner instruction 2026-11-09, add all of it

rules.text: No comments on reposts, because a repost carries no author argument to answer and a substantive comment under one is a broadcast. The single exception is a repost that carries the author's own writing around it, which is recorded in the file as the author's argument. The held-file pattern already exists for these; this makes it the rule rather than the habit.
rules.source: owner instruction 2026-11-09, add all of it

rules.text: Every post carries a real number, from a run that happened, or says in the text why it carries none. R06 still owns the figures: the number is real or it is absent, and absent-with-a-reason is the acceptable version of absent. A post that wants a number and has no run writes the method and says so.
rules.source: owner instruction 2026-11-09, add all of it; bounded by R06
